TCE 504 • Applied Exercise Physiology
04 / FOUNDATION
4 • FOOD → SUBSTRATES

Food becomes usable fuel.

Your body does not pour “energy” directly from food into the muscle. Food is digested into smaller molecules. Those molecules become substrates that can be stored, transported and metabolised to regenerate ATP.

Before you look at the pathway: What has to happen to food before a working muscle can use it?
SEE THE WHOLE PATHWAY Food → substrates → muscle → ATP production
Read the visual carefully: follow the different forms of carbohydrate, fat and protein from food to substrates, then to the muscle cell and mitochondria. Notice that the athlete application is already built into the visual.
Important: “Fuel selection” is not simply carbohydrate OR fat. Both can be oxidised simultaneously. Relative contribution changes with intensity, duration, training status and substrate availability.
STOP & THINK
Which statement best describes what happens to food before it can support ATP resynthesis in muscle?
NEXT → ENERGY & ATP
You have followed food into glucose, fatty acids and amino acids. Now we need to understand the immediate energy currency that the muscle continually uses and regenerates: ATP.
